rationale: flops-2 is a tiny (527-byte text, 2-function) pure floating-point compute kernel where essentially all execution time sits in one hot numeric loop, so the dominant constraint is runtime preservation: RuntimeCost weights are set high (0.85-0.95) across the board so hot-loop functions are shielded from expensive transforms. BCF and FLA are further suppressed via high SizeCost (0.9/0.85) because bogus blocks and dispatcher state machines bloat a 527-byte binary disproportionately relative to the marginal security they add to code with no secrets, algorithms, or licensing logic to protect; their CorrectnessRisk is also elevated because aggressive restructuring of FP-dominated loops can disturb scheduling and value semantics. SUB gets moderate Security/Diversity weight but the highest CorrectnessRisk (0.9) since arithmetic substitution on FP code risks changing rounding/NaN behavior and yields little benefit on float ops; if it applies, it should confine itself to integer address/index computations. SPLIT and IBR are kept as the middle ground — cheap, modest diversity gains on the small control flow — while ICALL and IGV are weighted toward disabling: with a single main function, no meaningful call graph to indirect, and almost no globals, they add indirect-call/dispatch overhead and debugging-hostile indirection with essentially zero reverse-engineering payoff. Net effect: the table permits only low-overhead diversity (SPLIT, occasional SUB on integer code, light IBR) and effectively vetoes the heavy structural passes, which is the right trade for a benchmark stub whose RE value is minimal and whose runtime fidelity is the point.
